title: Historical Glasgow structure likened to 'UFO' granted B-listed status
excerpt: Cranhill Water Tower in the East End of Glasgow has been granted listed status by Historic Environment Scotland.
content:
A historical structure in the East End of Glasgow which has previously been likened to a UFO has been granted listed status.

The Cranhill Water Tower, which has stood in the area since 1951, has been given category B listed status by Historic Environment Scotland (HES).

(Image: Colin Mearns, Newsquest)

(Image: Newsquest)

It comes after an appeal was lodged by Labour MSP Paul Sweeney earlier this year, who said it was important to protect the structure of the tower and preserve its history. A public consultation was thereafter opened by HES.

Speaking on the news, Sweeney said: "I am delighted that Historic Environment Scotland has confirmed Cranhill Water Tower will be listed at Category B and in doing so has recognised its special architectural and historic interest.

"Earlier this year I nominated this striking 1951 structure, because it is far more than a disused piece of infrastructure. Designed by Frank A Macdonald and Partners for Glasgow Corporation, it was built to serve the new post-war housing scheme and remains the earliest surviving example of its kind in the city. Now, they symbolise the ambition and confidence of Glasgow's post-war planning, a period when the city built new communities with real vision.

"Category B listing gives this building the statutory protection it deserves so that future generations can appreciate our twentieth-century heritage as much as our Victorian treasures. With the right care we can restore the architectural lighting that once made the tower such a distinctive night-time feature and ensure it continues to stand as a proud landmark for Cranhill and the wider East End.

"I want to thank Historic Environment Scotland for recognising its special architectural and historic interest, and the Twentieth Century Society for their support throughout."

(Image: Colin Mearns, Newsquest)

The water tower is a 25m tall Brutalist structure designed by Frank A Macdonald and Partners for Glasgow Corporation.

HES have legally exclude artist Andy Scott's Neptune Project sculptures found at the base of the tower from the listing.

A spokesperson for HES said: "Following a public consultation, we have listed Cranhill Water Tower at Category B.

"Located at the eastern edge of Cranhill housing estate, it is the earliest known post-war water tower to survive in Glasgow. Built in 1951 and designed by Frank A Macdonald and Partners for Glasgow Corporation, the Water Tower is a major example from the unrivalled programme of reinforced concrete water tower construction in Glasgow and its environs during the 1950s and 60s."

(Image: Colin Mearns, Newsquest)

(Image: Colin Mearns, Newsquest)

The building has now been passed over to Scottish Water, who own the structure. A spokesperson told the Glasgow Times that they have no immediate plans at this time.
